vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2407: feat(cli): one paved-road verb to take an issue from any state to running work — collapse the plan/--auto/--auto-start flag maze

plan.title: feat(cli): one paved-road verb to take an issue from any state to running work — collapse the plan/--auto/--auto-start flag maze
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Getting an issue moving requires a 2-verb × 3-flag matrix (pan plan / --auto / --auto-start / pan start --auto). Worse, pan start on an unplanned issue silently creates one generic bead instead of planning. Operators must know three entry points for one intent: 'get this issue moving' plus a planning-depth choice.
narratives.Proposal: Make pan start <id> the paved road: no plan → kick off planning at the configured depth via the existing start-planning endpoint with the autoSpawnOnFinalize stamp so work starts automatically on finalize; plan exists → spawn work (unchanged); already running → no-op with a clear message and exit 0. Planning depth becomes one dial: --plan interactive|auto|skip, defaulting to new config key planning.default_mode (shipped default 'auto'). pan start --auto becomes a deprecated alias of --plan skip; pan plan --auto-start prints a deprecation pointer. Skills and CLAUDE.md updated in the same change.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No dashboard UI changes (PlanDialog, kanban Plan/Auto-plan actions keep their payloads)
- No changes to the start-planning or start-agent server route contracts
- No removal of pan plan, pan plan --auto, pan plan --auto-start, or pan start --auto (deprecation warnings only)
- No removal of the single-generic-bead fallback in start.ts:1239-1261
- No migration of flywheel/orchestrator call sites to the new surface (old flags keep working)
- No changes to remote (Fly.io) workspace spawn behavior beyond passing workspaceLocation through to start-planning

autoDecisions.summary: Reuse the dashboard start-planning endpoint for pan start's auto-plan routing instead of a new CLI-side planning spawn path.
autoDecisions.rationale: pan plan already POSTs /api/issues/:id/start-planning with auto/autoStart and the autoSpawnOnFinalize stamp already drives work spawn on finalize; one spawn path keeps single-source-of-truth and requires zero server changes.
The issue body names 'shipped default auto' explicitly; auto-planning is the defensible middle between interactive (blocks on a human) and skip (no real plan).

autoDecisions.summary: Precedence: --plan flag > legacy --auto (maps to 'skip') > planning.default_mode > 'auto'; --plan wins over --auto with a warning when both are passed.
autoDecisions.rationale: Explicit new dial beats deprecated alias beats config beats shipped default — standard CLI precedence; erroring on the combination would break scripts mid-deprecation-window.
The issue specifies 'Q&A session first, then continues to work on approval' — the auto-start stamp is exactly that continuation.

autoDecisions.summary: pan start on an already-running work agent exits 0 with an informative message; paused/troubled keep exit 1.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for 'no-op with a clear message'; the paved-road intent (get it moving) is already satisfied, so success is truthful. Paused/troubled require operator action, so failure remains correct there.

autoDecisions.summary: Plan existence is detected via findPlanSync(workspace) when a workspace exists, else pan-dir findSpecByIssue(projectRoot, issueId); any found spec counts regardless of status.
autoDecisions.rationale: Mirrors the pipeline's canonical spec resolution (PAN-1124 single-spec-on-main); re-planning completed/cancelled issues is pan reopen's job, not pan start's.

autoDecisions.summary: planning.default_mode is validated at the consumption site (resolver exits 1 naming key and valid values on an invalid value), not at config load.
autoDecisions.rationale: Config load stays resilient for unrelated commands; the failure is loud exactly where the value is used — consistent with the no-silent-fallback rule.

autoDecisions.summary: The single-generic-bead fallback in start.ts stays in place even though the paved road makes it unreachable for unplanned local issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: Additive-refactor/no-loss rule: deleting a reachable-in-edge-cases behavior needs its own audit; retention is zero-risk.

autoDecisions.summary: Deprecations are warn-only in this issue; no flags are removed.
autoDecisions.rationale: Issue acceptance explicitly requires pan plan --auto --auto-start to keep working with a pointer; removal is a future issue after the window.

autoDecisions.summary: Dry-run on an unplanned issue prints the intended planning route and exits before any POST.
autoDecisions.rationale: Naive routing would make --dry-run actually spawn a planning session — a side effect dry-run must never have.

Unset = 'auto'. */ default_mode?: 'interactive' | 'auto' | 'skip' }`. Thread the section through the config load/merge path (src/lib/config-yaml/domain-mergers.ts and defaults.ts follow the pattern of other optional sections — copy how a small section like compliance or resources is merged). Keep the raw value as-typed; do NOT validate or coerce at load time — per decision D7 validation happens in the pan start resolver (see item plan-mode-flag). Write a unit test (new file src/lib/config-yaml/__tests__/planning-config.test.ts, or extend an existing config-yaml test file if the directory convention prefers that) covering: value round-trips from YAML, and absent section leaves planning undefined.

narrative.Action: In issueCommand (src/cli/commands/start.ts:856), after the paused/troubled gates and before workspace creation / remote handling (before the findWorkspaceWithLocation block around line 941): detect plan existence per decision D6 — if a workspace exists use findPlanSync(workspace) (src/lib/vbrief/io.ts); otherwise use findSpecByIssue(projectRoot, issueId) from src/lib/pan-dir/specs.ts:216 via Effect.runPromise, or add and use a sync export mirroring the private findSpecByIssueSync (src/lib/vbrief/io.ts:48). projectRoot comes from findProjectRoot(id) (start.ts:564). THEN: (a) plan exists → fall through to the existing spawn path completely unchanged (FR-8). (b) No plan and resolved mode is 'auto' or 'interactive' → if options.dryRun, print 'Would start <mode> planning session for <id> (work agent auto-starts on finalize)' and return without any HTTP request (FR-9); otherwise POST `${getDashboardApiUrlSync()}/api/issues/<ID>/start-planning` with JSON body { auto: mode === 'auto', autoStart: true, probe: false, model, harness, effort, workspaceLocation: options.remote ? 'remote' : 'local' } — the same body shape planCommand sends (src/cli/commands/plan.ts:26-38) — and stream the SSE progress events exactly as planCommand's reader loop does (plan.ts:53-84). Extract that reader loop into a shared helper (new src/cli/commands/planning-stream.ts or an export from plan.ts) so the two commands cannot drift; planCommand must be refactored to call the same helper. On success print a completion line stating the planning session name and that the work agent will start automatically after planning finalizes. On connection failure (dashboard down) print an error pointing at 'pan up' and '--plan skip' for offline use, exit 1 (hazard H1). (c) No plan and mode 'skip' → set the existing options.auto synthesized-vBRIEF path in motion unchanged (start.ts:1215-1232 writeAutoStartVBrief + createBeadsFromVBrief); no deprecation warning for skip-via---plan (FR-4). Do NOT touch the single-generic-bead fallback at start.ts:1239-1261 (decision D8). Tests (src/cli/commands/__tests__/start-plan-routing.test.ts): mock fetch and the spec/plan lookup; assert request body per mode ({auto:true,autoStart:true} for auto; {auto:false,autoStart:true} for interactive), assert no fetch for plan-exists and for dry-run, assert skip path calls writeAutoStartVBrief and never fetches start-planning. Follow existing start.ts test-mocking patterns (see start-harness.test.ts). Repo rule: no real timers/sleeps — mock the SSE stream; use vi.useFakeTimers() if anything delay-based appears.

narrative.Action: In issueCommand (src/cli/commands/start.ts:856), after the paused/troubled gates (lines 908-925) add an explicit liveness check: use getWorkAgentLifecycleStateSync (src/lib/work-agent-lifecycle.ts) — or sessionExistsSync from src/lib/tmux.js as the existing --fresh path does at line 965 — to determine whether agent-<id> has a live running session. If running, print a message that (1) states the work agent for <ID> is already running, (2) names `pan tell <id> "..."` for messaging and `tmux -L overdeck attach -t agent-<id>` for attaching, and return with exit code 0 (process.exitCode = 0, plain return — not process.exit(1)). Today this case throws from assertCanStartFreshSync (start.ts:984) and exits 1; the change scopes the exit-0 no-op STRICTLY to the live-running state (hazard H2). Paused agents keep the existing exit-1 refusal (start.ts:909-916); troubled agents keep exit-1 (start.ts:917-925); a stopped agent with a resumable session keeps the existing refusal pointing at pan resume/--fresh. Test in src/cli/commands/__tests__/start-running-noop.test.ts mocks the lifecycle/tmux lookups and asserts the exit codes and message content for running vs paused.
